prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I'm looking for any bottle of wine that costs less than 15 euros, can you help me find one?"

List A:
Wine 1: Merlot, US, $15. Tasting note: "A nice Bordeaux style wine for fifteen bucks. It's dry and firmly tannic, with black currant and cola flavors, and some elegance. Fine now with a steak or chop."
Wine 2: Red Blend, Italy, $60. Tasting note: "Guidoalberto is the “pocketbook-friendly” alternative from the same estate that makes Sassicaia. But for $60, you could ask for more. This is a chewy, succulent wine with good length on the close. The aromas are awkward in places with espresso, chocolate yogurt and a touch of cheese rind."
Wine 3: Pinot Noir, US, $20. Tasting note: "A pretty good Pinot that, at the equivalent of 10 bucks a bottle, is a nice buy. It's an easy wine, dry, light-bodied and silky, with modest cherry and spice flavors."
Wine 4: Muskat Ottonel, Austria, $15. Tasting note: "Often used to make Austrian sweet wines, Muskat Ottonel here is an off-dry wine. The wine brings out the perfumed character of the grape, a simple, full and ripe wine that has rough edges. Screwcap."
Wine 5: Cabernet Sauvignon, South Africa, $15. Tasting note: "For $15, this is a good value wine with a solid structure and nice balance. Black currant flavors steal the show in the mouth, with supporting notes of whole star anise, cigar tobacco and cedary spice on the finish."

List B:
Wine 1: Red Blend, South Africa, $65. Tasting note: "A limited production wine (only 3,440 bottles produced) that has the depth and concentration one would expect for a wine with this price tag. Dark and floral with aromas of crushed African violets, black plum, cherry and clover. The mouth is lush and velvety, loaded with flavors of cassis, black berry, pepper and leathery spice that continue through the finish. Drink now through 2015."
Wine 2: Cabernet Sauvignon, South Africa, $15. Tasting note: "For $15, this is a good value wine with a solid structure and nice balance. Black currant flavors steal the show in the mouth, with supporting notes of whole star anise, cigar tobacco and cedary spice on the finish."
Wine 3: Red Blend, Argentina, $15. Tasting note: "Here's a Bordeaux-style blend to snap up if you're lucky enough to find it. It's a definite re-issue in that it was first released at $25 in 2006 but was put back on the market last year at $15. And what a bargain it is: Earth, tar and tobacco vie with dried cherry and raspberry on the nose and palate; the finish is long, elegant and dry. A mature, classy wine to drink now."
Wine 4: Pinot Noir, US, $14. Tasting note: "The price is right, but the wine is ordinary. It's a modest little Pinot Noir, silky and dry, with suggestions of cherries, tangerine peel and cola."
Wine 5: Cabernet Sauvignon, France, $8. Tasting note: "This wine is quite the bargain, offering nice fruit and spice for under $10. Simply structured with soft tannins, juicy black currant and plum flavors all accented by a hint of pepper. Drink now."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
